AFM Ferojuddin Bhuiyan, Advocate ----- For the Applicant. 
Dabiruddin Ahmed, Deputy Attorney-General ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Mukta Biri Factory Ltd ------ Petitioner
vs
Commissioner of Taxes ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
"(a) Whether the Taxes Appellate Tribunal Division Bench-1, Dhaka was justified in law in upholding the dismissal of Appeal as barred by limitation at the back of the assesse without pointing it out to the assesse of the fact of the delay. 

 The applicant assesse is manufacturer of Biri's which filed a return for the assessment year 1989-90 showing loss of Taka 6,11,500.00. The income tax officer assessed income at Taka 26,50,771.00. Being aggrieved by the assessment order the assesse preferred an appeal before the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) Zone-3, Dhaka. The Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) vide an order dated 9-2-93 dismissed the appeal in liming on the ground of limitation. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) the assesse took a second appeal being ITA No. 1902 of 1993-94 before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Division Bench-1, Dhaka and the Appellate Tribunal by the impugned Judgment affirmed the order of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) and the instant reference application is directed against that order. 

 3. Mr AFM Ferojuddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the applicant, submits that in the instant case the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) dismissed the appeal on the ground of limitation without giving any opportunity, to the applicant to explain the delay. The learned Advocate referring to section 154(3) of the Ordinance submits that the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) was empowered by sub-section-3 of section 154 of the Ordinance to admit an appeal after the expiration of the period of limitation if he is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient causes from presenting the appeal within the prescribed period of limitation and the said sub-section casts a duty upon the appellate forum to give a chance to the appellant to explain the delay. But in the facts and circumstances of the case without giving any opportunity to the appellant of being heard on the point of limitation, the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) illegally dismissed the appeal in limine and the Appellate Tribunal in affirming the order of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) also did not advert to this legal aspect of the case and they also did not give any opportunity to the applicant to explain the delay and thereby illegally dismissed the appeal, the learned Advocate further submits. 

 4. Mr Dabiruddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondent, submits that in the instant case the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) dismissed the appeal on the point of limitation after hearing the parties as would be evident from the impugned order itself and thereby the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) did not commit any illegality in dismissing the appeal on the point of limitation. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that section 154(3) of the Ordinance empowers the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) to admit an appeal beyond the period of limitation if sufficient cause is shown by the appellant but in the instant case no cause was shown by the appellant as to what prevented from filing the appeal in time and thus the Appellate Tribunal rightly dismissed the appeal. 

 5. We have perused the application and the relevant orders annexed therewith and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates of both the parties. On perusal of the order of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) it does not appear that he had given any opportunity to the applicant to explain his position and the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) relying on the materials available on the record found that the appeal was barred by limitation and, as such, dismissed the same. It appears that in view of sub-section (3) of section 154 of the Ordinance the Appellate forum was under a legal obligation to give an opportunity to the applicant to explain the delay and reasons of satisfaction and non-satisfaction ought to have been recorded by him in the order but it appears that no such reasons have been recorded by the Commissioner Taxes (Appeal) and the Order dated 9-2-93 does not show if any opportunity was given to the assesse to explain the delay. It appears that the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) on such technical ground dismissed the appeal as barred by limitation on the back of the assesse and thereby deprived the assesse of the chance to explain the delay and to file an application for condo nation of delay. On a perusal of the impugned order it appears that the Appellate Tribunal also dismissed the appeal and affirmed the order of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) but in affirming the order the Appellate Tribunal also lost sight of sub-section (3) of section 154 of the Ordinance and they also did not give any opportunity to the appellant to explain the delay in preferring the appeal before the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal). Thus it appears that the impugned order in affirming the order in the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) suffers from illegality and infirmity and the assesse applicant ought to have been given a chance by the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) to explain the delay in filing the appeal. In the instant case, in our opinion, the ends of justice would have been met if a direction was given by the Tribunal to the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) to hear the appeal after giving an opportunity to the assesse to explain the delay. It appears to us that in view of the provisions of sub-section (3) of section 154 of the Ordinance the assesse applicant ought to have been given an opportunity to explain the delay in preferring the appeal before the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) and such consideration of the causes shown should be reflected in the appellate order. But in the present case the assesse applicant had been illegally deprived of that opportunity by the Hosne Ara Begum Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal). We are others, 43 DLR 543 ref. therefore, of the view that the order dated 9-2-93 of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) and the impugned order offends the provision of sub-section 3 of section 154 of the Ordinance. Thus, we answer the question No (a) in the negative and in favour of the assesse. The applicant did not press question Nos. (b) and (c) as formulated in paragraph No. 8 of the application and accordingly, we need not give any opinion on those two questions. Here it may be mentioned that the statement of facts made in this reference application has neither been denied nor controverted by the respondent by filing a written reply and, as such, statements of facts made by the applicant in this reference must be taken to be true.
